<!-- All news items below this line -->{{Current events|year=2005|month=09|day=25|content=

* American psychiatrist and best-selling author [[M. Scott Peck]], M.D. dies after suffering from [[Parkinson's disease]] and [[pancreatic]] and liver duct [[cancer]].  Peck, 69, was the author of ''The Road Less Traveled''.  [https://www.nytimes.com/2005/09/28/books/28peck.html (New York Times)], [https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=4868067 (NPR)]
* [[2005 northern Peru earthquake]]: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake, the strongest in the country in four years, strikes northern [[Peru]], with at least four persons reported dead. [http://www.cnn.com/2005/WORLD/americas/09/26/peru.quake/index.html (CNN)]
* [[Renault in Formula One|Renault]] driver [[Fernando Alonso]] becomes the youngest ever [[Formula One]] champion when finishing 3rd behind [[McLaren]] rivals [[Juan Pablo Montoya]] and [[Kimi Räikkönen]] in the [[2005 Brazilian Grand Prix]] at age 24. [https://web.archive.org/web/20060410091318/http://www.f1racing.net/en/news.php?newsID=99343 (F1Racing.net)]
* [[Polish parliamentary election, 2005]]: As predicted by polls, support for Prime Minister Marek Belka's post-communist [[Democratic Left Alliance (Poland)|Democratic Left Alliance]] drops sharply to about 11%, while center-right opposition  parties [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] and [[Civic Platform]] will obtain about 28% and 26%, respectively. [http://wiadomosci.onet.pl/1169261,11,item.html (onet.pl <nowiki>[Polish]</nowiki>)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/4279562.stm (BBC)]
* Swiss voters approve a [[referendum]] by 56% to 44% to allow citizens from the 10 newest [[European Union]] member countries to travel and work in Switzerland. Quotas will be applied until [[2011]] on the number of people allowed to settle. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/4280462.stm (BBC)]
* [[Conflict in Iraq]]: 
** At least four [[Shia]] Muslims, believed to be members of the [[Mahdi Army]] are killed by US soldiers in a gunfight following a U.S. raid into [[Sadr City]], eastern [[Baghdad]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/4279988.stm (BBC)]
** Nine people die following a bomb attack on a police station in [[Hillah]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/4279988.stm (BBC)]
* [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|Conflict in Afghanistan]]: 5 US soldiers die when a [[Boeing CH-47 Chinook|Chinook]] helicopter crashes in [[Zabul]], southern [[Afghanistan]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/4279858.stm (BBC)]
* Over 100,000 people attend anti-Iraq War rally held in Washington, D.C. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/4278960.stm (BBC)]
* [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]:
** The [[Israel Defense Forces]] launch Operation First Rain, a series of air strikes on [[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] targets in the [[Gaza Strip]], including an alleged [[Hamas]] weapons factory and a children's school. According to Israel the operation's goal is to stop shelling of southern [[Israel]]i towns and villages by Palestinian militants, though several civilians have been injured, including an infant. At least 200 Palestinians have been arrested in overnight [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] raids in the [[West Bank]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/4280262.stm (BBC)] [http://www.guardian.co.uk/worldlatest/story/0,1280,-5301572,00.html (The Guardian)] [http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3146657,00.html (YNETnews)] [https://web.archive.org/web/20060220171044/http://english.aljazeera.net/NR/exeres/5E9E8634-35C4-4F72-BD41-D1A1C3B50C83.htm (Al Jazeera)]
* [[EuroBasket 2005]]: [[Greece]] beats Germany 78 to 62 and wins for the second time in its history the Eurobasket.
